sections.title: Introduction to Salvation
observations: Peter opens his letter by addressing the recipients as 'elect exiles' which emphasizes their identity in Christ and their temporary status in this world.
The concept of being chosen by God is central to Reformed theology, highlighting God's sovereignty in salvation.

sections.title: The Living Hope
observations: Peter speaks of a 'living hope' through the resurrection of Jesus Christ, which is foundational for Christian faith.
This hope is not just a future expectation but a present reality that sustains believers through trials.

sections.title: The Call to Holiness
observations: Peter urges believers to be holy as God is holy, reflecting the character of God in their lives.
This call to holiness is rooted in the understanding of their redemption and the cost paid by Christ.

sections.title: The Enduring Word of God
observations: The chapter concludes with a reminder of the imperishable nature of God's Word compared to the fleeting nature of human life.
This serves as an encouragement to rely on God's promises and truth amidst life's challenges.

importantVerses.commentary: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ! According to his great mercy, he has caused us to be born again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead.
You shall be holy, for I am holy.

questions: What does it mean to be an 'elect exile' in today's context?
How does the concept of 'living hope' influence our daily lives as Christians?
In what ways can we pursue holiness in a culture that often opposes it?
How does understanding the imperishable nature of God's Word affect our approach to Scripture?
